title: The Condemned
full_review:
Posing as a commentary on the entertainment industry -- and the viewing habits it fosters --"The Condemned" (Lionsgate), showcases extreme violence and inhuman behavior.

The action picture, produced by World Wrestling Entertainment, does indeed incorporate debate about the issues at hand, but that doesn't let the film off the hook for the rampant brutality pictured on screen.

Hoping to snare more viewers than the Super Bowl, greedy television producer Breck (Robert Mammone) stages a heinous reality event. He plucks 10 "expendable" contestants from death rows in Third-World prisons and drops them on a tropical island for a 30-hour fight to the death recorded by 400 cameras and streamed online live.

Breck rigs them with explosive ankle bracelets and cruelly manipulates the proceedings. Conrad, a U.S. Special Forces operative played by "Stone Cold" Steve Austin, is the putative hero, though it's impossible to root for anyone. After eight of the players are dispatched, Conrad faces off against barbaric Briton McStarley (Vinnie Jones). A huge Web audience tunes in to the blood sport.

Director and co-writer Scott Wiper tries to have it both ways by presenting depraved material and criticizing those who peddle it. This reflexivity comes off as cynical and is arguably more pernicious than what actually transpires.

At least ultraviolent horror movies like "Saw" and "Hostel" are honest about their intention to shock and revolt. Perhaps "The Condemned" may spur discussion about media violence, the only possible benefit of this sadistic film.

The film contains pervasive brutal violence and degrading situations, including torture and rape, pervasive rough and crude language and some profanity. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted. Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian.
